items.passage: Coins rattled in the ticket machine as Maeve fed it, one at a time, refusing my help. My sister had been home from her deployment for nine days, and the metro platform in Galway was the farthest she had gone alone. On the radio that morning, a man who had served in her unit described the night their convoy was struck: smoke, shouting, a corporal carried out by Maeve herself. At breakfast, Maeve had told it differently. No one carried anyone, she said; the corporal walked, and she only held the door. I have wondered which of them is lying. But watching her now, counting the coins twice and pressing each one in as though it might be refused, I think the question is the wrong one. Perhaps she remembers holding the door because that is the part she can bear to have done.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Maeve?
options: She is openly skeptical of Maeve's account and resents her for contradicting the radio.
She is amused by Maeve's stubbornness and treats her return home as a minor event.
She is fearful of Maeve's changed temper and avoids speaking to her about the war.
She is tenderly perceptive, moving from doubt toward compassion for Maeve's memory.
items.explanation: 화자 Brigid는 처음에 라디오 증언과 언니의 말 중 누가 거짓말을 하는지 궁금해한다. 그러나 동전을 두 번 세며 조심스럽게 넣는 Maeve를 지켜보며 그 질문 자체가 잘못되었다고 생각한다. 마지막 문장에서는 Maeve가 견딜 수 있는 부분만 기억하는 것일 수 있다고 이해하려 한다. 따라서 의심에서 연민으로 나아가는 섬세한 태도인 D가 정답이며, A는 처음의 의심만 보고 원망까지 덧붙인 오답이다.

items.passage: After the storm, the stairwell of the old block on Wilmslow Road in Manchester smelled of wet plaster, and a section of wall beside the third landing had slumped away to reveal a small tin box wedged between the bricks. Tunde found it first. He was a man who announced everything, his cholesterol, the council's failings, the proper way to fold a shirt, and yet he slipped the box into his coat without a word. Dana, his son, who had not visited in a year and had come only because the power was out, watched him do it and said nothing either. They were alike in that, though neither would have admitted it; they had argued about who was more stubborn for most of Dana's life. Later, in the flat, Tunde opened the box at the kitchen table: a child's tooth, a hospital bracelet, a photograph of a boy on these same stairs. He pushed it across to Dana as though returning something borrowed.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Tunde and Dana?
options: Wry yet affectionate, noting their shared stubbornness and their hidden tenderness.
Harshly critical, blaming both men for allowing the old building to fall into disrepair.
Coolly detached, recording their actions without suggesting any feeling between them.
Openly sentimental, praising Tunde as a model father whom Dana has unfairly neglected.
items.explanation: 서술자는 Tunde가 콜레스테롤부터 셔츠 개는 법까지 모든 것을 떠벌린다고 가볍게 비꼬고, 두 사람이 누가 더 고집이 센지 평생 다퉜다고 말한다. 동시에 아들의 어린 시절 물건이 든 상자를 조용히 건네는 장면으로 숨겨진 애정을 드러낸다. 따라서 재치 있으면서도 다정한 시선인 A가 정답이다. C는 감정이 전혀 없다고 했지만 마지막 장면과 맞지 않고, D는 서술자가 한쪽 편을 들지 않으므로 틀리다.

items.passage:
Nairobi sleeps below the old beacon tower
where no ship has ever needed light,
and still the lamp turns, and still we come,
Baraka and I, to the chess club in its base.
He plays the Sicilian, as he has for thirty years.
I play badly, as I have for thirty years,
and neither of us speaks of the winter
he paid my rent and asked for nothing back.
Some debts are coins. Some are a chair
pulled out for you every Thursday,
a kettle already warm, a clock pressed
gently on your side when you are losing.
I have tried to repay it. He will not take it.
So I lose to him slowly, with great care,
and he pretends each time to be surprised.
items.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward Baraka?
options: Resentful, because Baraka keeps reminding the speaker of the money he is still owed.
Grateful and fond, expressing an unspoken obligation through their ritual of play.
Competitive and bitter, determined at last to defeat Baraka after years of losing.
Indifferent, treating the weekly chess games as a habit with no deeper meaning.
items.explanation: 화자는 Baraka가 겨울에 집세를 내 주고 아무것도 요구하지 않았다고 말하며, 둘 다 그 일을 입에 올리지 않는다고 밝힌다. 또 의자를 빼 주고 주전자를 데워 두는 등의 작은 친절도 빚으로 여기며 갚으려 했지만 거절당했다고 한다. 그래서 정성껏 천천히 져 주는 체스 의식으로 고마움을 표현한다. 따라서 B가 정답이며, A는 두 사람 모두 빚을 언급하지 않는다는 내용과 반대이다.

items.passage: On the first Tuesday of every month, I collected my younger brother Wolfram from the reading room of a quiet library near the Ringstrasse in Vienna, where his tutor, Anselm, taught him geography from maps older than our grandparents. I disliked Anselm at first. He was late, he hummed, and he insisted that Wolfram learn to walk home by landmarks rather than by the tram map I had drawn for him. I thought it was vanity, an old man's romance with the city. Then one winter evening the trams stopped in a snowstorm. I found Wolfram already halfway home, steering by the green dome of a church, the bakery with the brass pretzel, the fountain with the missing nose. He had not needed my map at all. I still think Anselm hums too much. But I no longer think his lessons were for show, and I have started, a little grudgingly, to notice landmarks myself.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Anselm?
options: Unchanged dislike, since the storm confirmed that his methods put Wolfram in danger.
Uncritical admiration, as she now regards him as the finest teacher in Vienna.
Reluctant respect, as she comes to value his methods despite lingering annoyance.
Amused indifference, as she treats his lessons as harmless but ultimately pointless.
items.explanation: 필자는 처음에 Anselm이 늦고 콧노래를 부르며 허영심으로 랜드마크 학습을 고집한다고 싫어했다. 그러나 눈보라로 트램이 멈춘 날 Wolfram이 랜드마크만으로 집에 오는 모습을 보고 그의 방법이 옳았음을 인정한다. 그럼에도 여전히 콧노래가 지나치다고 말하며 '조금 마지못해' 랜드마크를 보기 시작했다고 한다. 따라서 남은 불만 속의 마지못한 존중인 C가 정답이며, B는 비판이 남아 있다는 점을 놓쳤다.

items.passage: Three things I owed Katharina when I saw her again at my cousin's wedding in Hamburg: forty euros, a wool hat, and the two days of my life she had given back to me on a ridge in the Harz, when I was lost and stubborn and too proud to call for help. She was a park ranger then, impatient and sunburned, and she had lent me the money for the bus home without asking my name. Now she was a guest at the next table, laughing too loudly at a toast. I had rehearsed a gracious speech. Instead I pushed through the crowded hall holding a fifty-euro note and stammered something about interest. She looked at the money, then at me, and asked whether I still hiked alone. I admitted that I did. She folded the note back into my hand. 'Then you'll need the bus fare,' she said, and I was too grateful, and too embarrassed, to argue.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Katharina?
options: Resentful, because Katharina humiliates the narrator by refusing her money in public.
Nostalgic, longing to return to the ranger's life that Katharina once described.
Suspicious, since the narrator doubts that Katharina truly remembers the rescue.
Indebted and admiring, yet self-conscious about how to repay Katharina's kindness.
items.explanation: 필자는 처음부터 Katharina에게 진 빚을 돈, 모자, 되찾은 이틀이라는 목록으로 나열하며 큰 은혜를 느낀다. 준비한 연설 대신 말을 더듬으며 돈을 내미는 장면은 어떻게 갚아야 할지 몰라 쑥스러워하는 모습을 보여 준다. 마지막에 너무 고맙고 너무 부끄러워 반박하지 못했다는 말이 이를 확인한다. 따라서 D가 정답이며, A는 부끄러움을 원망으로 잘못 읽은 오답이다.

items.passage:
Joaquin, I am writing from the bench outside my father's ticket booth at the ferry terminal in Seville, where you stood last Sunday and asked me, quite seriously, how people here say goodbye. I laughed at you then, and I am sorry, but you must understand that nobody had ever asked me before. You had a list from a guidebook: the kiss on each cheek, the handshake, the wave from the deck. You wanted to do it properly. I told you there was no proper way, which was unkind, because there is, and you found it without me. When the horn sounded, you did not kiss or wave. You simply stood at the rail until the ferry turned the bend, the last passenger still facing the dock. My father says only fishermen and homesick people do that. I hope you will write and tell me which you are.

Marisol
items.question: Which choice best describes Marisol's attitude toward Joaquin?
options: Gently amused yet touched, coming to admire his sincere farewell.
Mildly irritated, finding his guidebook questions tiresome and naive.
Deeply suspicious, doubting that he truly intended to leave Seville.
Formally polite, offering travel advice as part of her father's business.
items.explanation: Marisol은 Joaquin의 진지한 질문에 웃었다고 고백하며 그의 안내서 목록을 가볍게 묘사한다. 그러나 그가 배 난간에 서서 끝까지 부두를 바라본 모습을 '제대로 된 방식'을 스스로 찾은 것이라고 인정한다. 마지막에 그가 어떤 사람인지 편지로 알려 달라는 말에서 애정 어린 관심이 드러난다. 따라서 A가 정답이며, B는 처음의 웃음을 짜증으로 오해했고 C와 D는 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Who decides which child stays behind when the olives must be carried down? So the old tellers on the terraces above Naples begin this tale. A young teacher named Emilio came to the hill school and announced that the slowest reader would stay to tend the trees while the others went to market. Alessia, who read slowly but counted quickly, folded her arms and said nothing. On market day Emilio found the baskets tallied wrong and the prices muddled, for no one else could reckon so well, and he climbed back up the hill red-faced to fetch her. The tellers say he never again chose by a single measure, though they add, with a wink, that he took a long time to admit it aloud. Even now, grandmothers who repeat the story pause here to slice bread, and the children wait, chins on hands, for the ending they already know.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Emilio?
options: Openly scornful, presenting him as a fool who never learns from his error
Deeply admiring, presenting his choice as wise from the very beginning
Gently amused, treating his mistake as forgivable while noting his pride
Coolly detached, reporting his actions without any hint of judgment
items.explanation: 서술자는 Emilio가 얼굴이 붉어진 채 언덕을 다시 올라왔다고 묘사하고, 그가 이후 하나의 기준으로 고르지 않았다고 하면서도 윙크와 함께 그것을 말로 인정하는 데 오래 걸렸다고 덧붙인다. 두 단서는 실수를 너그럽게 보면서도 자존심을 살짝 놀리는 태도를 보여 주므로 C가 정답이다. A는 그가 교훈을 얻었다는 서술과 어긋나고, B는 처음 선택이 틀렸던 점을 무시한다. D는 윙크 같은 평가적 표현이 있어 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Three clothespins per shirt, two per towel, one per sock: Ximena had hung her family's laundry by these rules on the Cairo rooftop since she was eight. Tariq, the landlord's son, liked to watch her count them out from the stairwell. One afternoon the wind came hard off the desert, and he ran up to help, pinning sheets any way he could, sometimes with four pins, sometimes with none. Ximena nearly scolded him. Instead she watched the sheets snap and hold, and she noticed that not one had fallen. The next week she left a few towels hanging by a single pin, just to see. They dried as quickly as the others. Below the roof, a vendor called out the price of guavas, and pigeons settled in a row along the water tank.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the passage?
options: A girl begins to loosen a strict routine after seeing it was less necessary than she believed.
A girl and a boy work together to keep the family laundry from blowing off a windy roof.
A boy learns from a girl the correct way to hang laundry so that it dries more quickly.
Helping one's neighbors during difficult weather is the best way to build a friendship.

items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Ximena는 여덟 살 때부터 정해진 개수의 빨래집게 규칙을 지켜 왔고, 바람 부는 날 Tariq이 아무렇게나 꽂은 시트가 하나도 떨어지지 않는 것을 본다. 뒷부분에서 그녀는 일부러 집게 하나로 수건을 걸어 보는데, 이 두 곳을 이으면 습관을 내려놓기 시작한다는 요지가 드러나 A가 정답이다. B는 일화만 요약했고, C는 배우는 사람을 뒤바꿔 목적이 다르다. D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Four trays of dough, two ovens, one hour before the doors open: that was the rule of the bakery in Kerala where Camille and I worked the summer after the storm. We had not spoken properly in years, Camille and I, though we kneaded at the same table. Kenji, the owner, assumed we were simply quiet people. Then the flood washed out the garden behind the shop and uncovered a tin box our grandmother had buried there, full of letters she had written to each of us and never sent. Camille read hers standing in the mud. I read mine by the ovens. Neither of us said what was inside. But the next morning she slid the sugar jar toward me before I asked for it, and I held the oven door for her tray. Kenji, noticing nothing, complained about the price of cardamom.
items.question: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the passage?
options: To describe the daily schedule that two sisters followed while working in a bakery
To explain how a storm destroyed the garden behind a small bakery in Kerala
To show two distant sisters taking a first, wordless step toward each other
To argue that family secrets should always be revealed before it is too late

items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자와 Camille은 같은 탁자에서 일하면서도 몇 년간 제대로 말하지 않았다고 하고, 뒷부분에서는 편지를 읽은 다음 날 말없이 설탕 병을 건네고 오븐 문을 잡아 준다. 두 곳의 대비를 이으면 소원했던 자매가 말없이 가까워지기 시작한다는 목적이 드러나 C가 정답이다. A는 일정만 다룬 소재 요약이고, B는 폭풍이라는 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르다. D는 지문이 주장하지 않는 일반적 교훈이다.

items.passage: Chalk dust and the smell of the harbor still drift through this classroom in Marseille, Remy, and I am writing to you from my desk during the break. You will laugh, but I am learning French verbs at seventy so that I can finally read the street signs I have walked past my whole life. When Theo first came to my fish stall, he was lost and could not read them either. I drew him a map on a scrap of wrapping paper, with a fish where my stall was and a star for his school. He still carries it, though he knows the way now. Last week he copied the street names for me into a notebook, slowly, letter by letter, and quizzed me as I sorted the mackerel. Tell your mother the boats came in late this morning, and the gulls were louder than the teacher.
items.question: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the letter?
options: To show how an old man and a boy have each guided the other in finding their way
To explain why the writer decided to sell fish near a language school in Marseille
To describe the route that Theo once followed from the fish stall to his school
To suggest that it is never too late for anyone to learn a new language or skill

items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 길을 잃은 Theo에게 포장지에 지도를 그려 주었고, 뒷부분에서는 Theo가 거리 이름을 공책에 베껴 주며 화자에게 퀴즈를 낸다. 두 일화를 이으면 노인과 소년이 서로에게 길잡이가 되어 준다는 목적이 드러나므로 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 없는 이유를 내세우고, C는 지도 일화만 요약한 것이다. D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: "You going to finish that boat, or just sit with it?" Devon called from the end of the dock. Amelie did not answer. The half-built skiff had rested on two sawhorses beside the lake for nine summers, ever since she and Devon had begun it together and then quarreled over the shape of the bow. Neither had touched it since, though both still walked past it most evenings. This evening Amelie had brought a plane and a jar of nails. She ran her hand along the bow, the curve Devon had wanted, and did not reshape it. When he came closer, she held out a second hammer, handle first, and waited. Out on the water, a heron lifted from the reeds and flew low toward the cypress trees.
items.question: Based on the passage, why does Amelie most likely hold out a second hammer to Devon?
options: She hopes to resume the shared project and mend the old quarrel with him.
She wants to prove that the boat's bow was built correctly from the start.
She is irritated by his remark and wants him to do the hardest work himself.
She needs the boat finished quickly before the lake's summer season ends.

items.explanation: 지문은 두 사람이 뱃머리 모양으로 다툰 뒤 아홉 해 동안 배를 건드리지 않았다고 밝히고, Amelie가 Devon이 원했던 곡선을 고치지 않은 채 쓰다듬는 장면을 보여 준다. 이 두 단서를 이으면 그녀가 화해하고 함께 작업을 이어 가려 한다는 동기가 드러나므로 A가 정답이다. B는 결과처럼 보이는 정당성 입증을 동기로 착각했고, C는 짜증이라는 다른 감정에서 나온 동기다. D는 지문에 없는 외부 시간 압박을 끌어왔다.

items.passage: Two buses an hour climbed past the stop on the ridge road outside Lagos, and Sergio had already let three of them go. The letter in his pocket offered him a place on a club in another city, where he would start every match instead of watching from the bench. Nneka, his coach, sat beside him on the concrete bench, saying nothing about it. She had benched him all season for missing practices, and he had called her unfair in front of the team. Yet that morning she had written to the other club herself, praising his speed and his footwork. Sergio had seen the copy on her desk. When the fourth bus came, he stood, shook her hand for a long moment, and boarded. Nneka watched it disappear around the bend, then walked back down to sweep the training field.
items.question: Based on the passage, why does Sergio most likely shake Nneka's hand for a long moment before boarding?
options: He wants to show her that he has forgiven her for keeping him on the bench all season.
He has realized she helped him get the offer, and he wishes to thank her for it.
He hopes the gesture will persuade her to let him return to the team's first lineup.
He is nervous about the new club and wants to delay leaving the familiar bus stop.

items.explanation: 지문은 Sergio가 코치를 불공평하다고 비난했던 과거를 밝힌 뒤, 그녀가 직접 상대 클럽에 추천서를 썼고 Sergio가 그 사본을 보았다고 서술한다. 두 단서를 이으면 그가 코치의 도움을 깨닫고 고마움을 표한다는 동기가 드러나므로 B가 정답이다. A는 용서라는 다른 감정에서 나온 동기이고, C는 그가 떠나는 결과와 맞지 않는 선발 복귀를 끌어왔다. D는 지문에 근거가 없는 불안을 동기로 내세웠다.

items.passage: When I was twelve, I broke my father's bicycle chain on a Dhaka curb and carried the pieces to Hari's shoe repair stall, because Hari could mend anything with leather and wire. I had already rehearsed a story about a careless rickshaw driver. Hari listened, nodding, then asked me to hold the chain while he worked. As he threaded each link, he told me how, as a boy, he had blamed a stray dog for a torn sandal and how his own father had believed him for thirty years. "He still mentions that dog," Hari said. "I have never had the courage to correct him." That evening I told my father the chain broke because I had jumped the curb too fast. He sighed, and then he laughed. Outside our window the street vendors were packing up their carts of mangoes for the night.
items.question: Based on the passage, why does Putri most likely tell her father the truth about the chain?
options: She fears that Hari will report the accident to her father if she does not.
She wants her father to laugh with her about how foolishly she had ridden.
She is upset that the rickshaw driver would be blamed and punished unfairly.
Hari's story shows her the lasting weight of a lie that is never corrected.

items.passage: Oaxaca was dry that March, and the river we crossed to reach my grandmother's village was only stones and cracked mud. Then she made me repeat his name three times, standing on the stones where the water used to be, until she was satisfied that I would not lose it. I did not understand her then. ### lit40-medium-01-075 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude

Coins rattled in the ticket machine as Maeve fed it, one at a time, refusing my help. My sister had been home from her deployment for nine days, and the metro platform in Galway was the farthest she had gone alone. On the radio that morning, a man who had served in her unit described the night their convoy was struck: smoke, shouting, a corporal carried out by Maeve herself. At breakfast, Maeve had told it differently. No one carried anyone, she said; the corporal walked, and she only held the door. I have wondered which of them is lying. But watching her now, counting the coins twice and pressing each one in as though it might be refused, I think the question is the wrong one. [질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Maeve?
A) She is openly skeptical of Maeve's account and resents her for contradicting the radio.
B) She is amused by Maeve's stubbornness and treats her return home as a minor event.

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
화자 Brigid는 처음에 라디오 증언과 언니의 말 중 누가 거짓말을 하는지 궁금해한다. 그러나 동전을 두 번 세며 조심스럽게 넣는 Maeve를 지켜보며 그 질문 자체가 잘못되었다고 생각한다. 마지막 문장에서는 Maeve가 견딜 수 있는 부분만 기억하는 것일 수 있다고 이해하려 한다. 따라서 의심에서 연민으로 나아가는 섬세한 태도인 D가 정답이며, A는 처음의 의심만 보고 원망까지 덧붙인 오답이다.

Tunde found it first. He was a man who announced everything, his cholesterol, the council's failings, the proper way to fold a shirt, and yet he slipped the box into his coat without a word. Dana, his son, who had not visited in a year and had come only because the power was out, watched him do it and said nothing either. They were alike in that, though neither would have admitted it; they had argued about who was more stubborn for most of Dana's life. 서술자는 Tunde가 콜레스테롤부터 셔츠 개는 법까지 모든 것을 떠벌린다고 가볍게 비꼬고, 두 사람이 누가 더 고집이 센지 평생 다퉜다고 말한다. 동시에 아들의 어린 시절 물건이 든 상자를 조용히 건네는 장면으로 숨겨진 애정을 드러낸다. 따라서 재치 있으면서도 다정한 시선인 A가 정답이다. C는 감정이 전혀 없다고 했지만 마지막 장면과 맞지 않고, D는 서술자가 한쪽 편을 들지 않으므로 틀리다.

On the first Tuesday of every month, I collected my younger brother Wolfram from the reading room of a quiet library near the Ringstrasse in Vienna, where his tutor, Anselm, taught him geography from maps older than our grandparents. I disliked Anselm at first. He was late, he hummed, and he insisted that Wolfram learn to walk home by landmarks rather than by the tram map I had drawn for him. I thought it was vanity, an old man's romance with the city. Then one winter evening the trams stopped in a snowstorm. I found Wolfram already halfway home, steering by the green dome of a church, the bakery with the brass pretzel, the fountain with the missing nose. He had not needed my map at all. I still think Anselm hums too much. But I no longer think his lessons were for show, and I have started, a little grudgingly, to notice landmarks myself.

[질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Anselm?

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
필자는 처음에 Anselm이 늦고 콧노래를 부르며 허영심으로 랜드마크 학습을 고집한다고 싫어했다. 그러나 눈보라로 트램이 멈춘 날 Wolfram이 랜드마크만으로 집에 오는 모습을 보고 그의 방법이 옳았음을 인정한다. 그럼에도 여전히 콧노래가 지나치다고 말하며 '조금 마지못해' 랜드마크를 보기 시작했다고 한다. 따라서 남은 불만 속의 마지못한 존중인 C가 정답이며, B는 비판이 남아 있다는 점을 놓쳤다.

Three things I owed Katharina when I saw her again at my cousin's wedding in Hamburg: forty euros, a wool hat, and the two days of my life she had given back to me on a ridge in the Harz, when I was lost and stubborn and too proud to call for help. She was a park ranger then, impatient and sunburned, and she had lent me the money for the bus home without asking my name. Now she was a guest at the next table, laughing too loudly at a toast. I had rehearsed a gracious speech. Instead I pushed through the crowded hall holding a fifty-euro note and stammered something about interest. She looked at the money, then at me, and asked whether I still hiked alone. I admitted that I did. She folded the note back into my hand. [질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Katharina?
A) Resentful, because Katharina humiliates the narrator by refusing her money in public.
B) Nostalgic, longing to return to the ranger's life that Katharina once described.
C) Suspicious, since the narrator doubts that Katharina truly remembers the rescue.
D) Indebted and admiring, yet self-conscious about how to repay Katharina's kindness.

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
필자는 처음부터 Katharina에게 진 빚을 돈, 모자, 되찾은 이틀이라는 목록으로 나열하며 큰 은혜를 느낀다. 준비한 연설 대신 말을 더듬으며 돈을 내미는 장면은 어떻게 갚아야 할지 몰라 쑥스러워하는 모습을 보여 준다. 마지막에 너무 고맙고 너무 부끄러워 반박하지 못했다는 말이 이를 확인한다. 따라서 D가 정답이며, A는 부끄러움을 원망으로 잘못 읽은 오답이다.
### lit40-medium-01-080 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]
Joaquin, I am writing from the bench outside my father's ticket booth at the ferry terminal in Seville, where you stood last Sunday and asked me, quite seriously, how people here say goodbye. I laughed at you then, and I am sorry, but you must understand that nobody had ever asked me before. You had a list from a guidebook: the kiss on each cheek, the handshake, the wave from the deck. You wanted to do it properly. I told you there was no proper way, which was unkind, because there is, and you found it without me. When the horn sounded, you did not kiss or wave. You simply stood at the rail until the ferry turned the bend, the last passenger still facing the dock. My father says only fishermen and homesick people do that. I hope you will write and tell me which you are.

[질문] Which choice best describes Marisol's attitude toward Joaquin?
A) Gently amused yet touched, coming to admire his sincere farewell.
B) Mildly irritated, finding his guidebook questions tiresome and naive.
C) Deeply suspicious, doubting that he truly intended to leave Seville.
D) Formally polite, offering travel advice as part of her father's business.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
Marisol은 Joaquin의 진지한 질문에 웃었다고 고백하며 그의 안내서 목록을 가볍게 묘사한다. 그러나 그가 배 난간에 서서 끝까지 부두를 바라본 모습을 '제대로 된 방식'을 스스로 찾은 것이라고 인정한다. 마지막에 그가 어떤 사람인지 편지로 알려 달라는 말에서 애정 어린 관심이 드러난다. 따라서 A가 정답이며, B는 처음의 웃음을 짜증으로 오해했고 C와 D는 근거가 없다.
### lit40-medium-01-082 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]

Alessia, who read slowly but counted quickly, folded her arms and said nothing. [질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Emilio?
A) Openly scornful, presenting him as a fool who never learns from his error
B) Deeply admiring, presenting his choice as wise from the very beginning

D) Coolly detached, reporting his actions without any hint of judgment

[해설]

### lit40-medium-01-084 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose

### lit40-medium-01-086 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
